original_question: Does the DNA of the BK virus encode a protein that regulates the transition of cells into the S phase of the cell cycle?

final_qi.question: Does the DNA of the BK virus encode a protein that regulates the transition of cells into the S phase of the cell cycle?
final_qi.long_answer: BK virus is a human polyomavirus. Like other polyomaviruses, its early-region DNA encodes the viral Large T antigen. Large T antigen binds and inactivates cellular retinoblastoma (pRb) family proteins and interacts with p53, thereby freeing E2F transcription factors and pushing the infected cell from G1 into S phase so that the virus can access the host’s DNA-replication machinery. Thus, the BK-virus genome does encode a protein that regulates (and promotes) the transition of cells into the S phase of the cell cycle.
